adaptation: Additive adaptation; never replace the polished original Teaching Stone episode.

storyCircle.you: Student in Mr. Hepting's classroom, invited to consider limited grain.
storyCircle.need: Make decisions that can be defended to people who must live with them.
storyCircle.go: Teaching Stone transports the student safely into an Egyptian village as a temporary adviser.
storyCircle.search: Hear needs, distribute rations, repair the bank, negotiate food and examine an accusation.
storyCircle.find: There are resources and workable plans, but each shifts a cost or risk.
storyCircle.take: The river tests preparation; evidence, labour debt and seed tradeoffs cannot be wished away.
storyCircle.return: Hand over responsibility and return safely through the stone.
storyCircle.change: Notice who an account omits; leave reasons, consequences and appeals open to scrutiny.

characterMotives.Djehu: Wants an accurate account; fears a correction will cost him his place. Open acknowledgment can teach a safer procedure.
characterMotives.Tia: Wants neighbours fed with dignity; knows absent and larger households disappear behind equal-looking totals.
characterMotives.Hori: Wants durable repairs without sacrificing workers' households; his father's failed patches explain his insistence on the foundation.
characterMotives.Intef: Wants people to survive and his contribution recognised; fears every future shortage becoming his personal obligation.

assessment: Four knowledge questions, 75/100 required. No moral points for a preferred decision or fortunate river outcome; independent Ethics portfolio preserved.
assets: Existing village scenery plus shared classroom; Hepting and four reusable cartoon-v1 character recipes. No new episode-specific player code.
curriculumBoundary: Faithful adaptation of the existing Egyptian lesson, rather than rewriting it into the current weekly Socrates unit.
availability: Separate published teacher-library edition. No original assignment or student attempt is changed.
